title: Canada Extends Work Permit Measures for Haitians and Sudanese to December 2027
excerpt: IRCC extended the temporary measures on the day they were set to expire, allowing eligible Haitian and Sudanese work permit holders in Canada to apply for extensions until December 30, 2027, with standard processing fees applying.
body:
• Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) has extended temporary work permit measures for Haitian and Sudanese nationals until December 30, 2027.
  • The extension was announced on October 27, 2026, the same day the measures had been set to expire.
  • To be eligible, a worker must hold a valid work permit issued under the previous temporary measures; standard processing fees apply to extension applications.
  • If you hold a Canadian work permit, applying to extend it before it expires preserves your right to keep working under the same conditions while IRCC decides — the maintained-status rule cited in the notice.

Canada's immigration department has extended measures providing work permits for Haitian and Sudanese nationals, according to a notice published in IRCC's online newsroom on October 27, 2026, reported by CIC News. The measures had been set to expire that same day and will now run until December 30, 2027.

Who Qualifies

The measures allow eligible foreign workers already in Canada to apply to extend their work permits. Eligibility is narrow: a foreign worker must hold a valid work permit issued under the previous temporary measures. Applications for extensions will be subject to standard processing fees, according to the notice.

https://x.com/CitImmCanada/status/2114809369007108580

Workers who apply before their existing permit expires benefit from maintained status, which authorizes them to continue working under the conditions of their existing permit until a decision is made on the application. That protection is the practical core of the extension: it prevents a gap in legal work authorization for people who cannot safely return to their home countries.

Background

IRCC first put temporary measures in place for Sudanese nationals in April 2023, after conflict erupted in Sudan; the measures were announced on April 24, 2023 and came into effect on April 30. Measures for Haitians followed on May 23, 2024, as Haiti's security crisis deepened. Both sets of measures were designed for nationals already in Canada who could not return home.

The extension, summarized in an IRCC update briefing for affected residents, also covers related temporary-resident options for the two groups, including visitor and student status options alongside work permits.

What Happens Next

Eligible permit holders should file extension applications before their current permits expire to keep maintained status. The December 30, 2027 end date now gives both groups more than a year of additional certainty, though the measures remain temporary public policy rather than a permanent immigration pathway, and IRCC can amend or end them with a further notice.

Why Temporary Measures Matter

Temporary measures of this kind are one of the main tools Canada uses when a crisis makes return unsafe: rather than creating a new immigration program, IRCC extends status for people already in the country under a public-policy exemption. The Haitian and Sudanese measures follow that pattern — they preserve work authorization for an existing group rather than opening a new route to Canada. For employers, the extension removes a near-term risk of losing staff whose permits were about to lapse. For the workers themselves, the critical detail is timing: an extension application filed before the current permit expires keeps the person in maintained status, while a permit that lapses first can interrupt the right to work until status is restored.
